title: Cross-stack technical deep dives
exp: These test system-level thinking across all tracks -- the questions that separate knows-the-tools from can-lead-a-platform-team.
pts: System design: clarify requirements, sketch happy path, identify one key decision, drill in, state trade-offs.
Schema versioning: additive changes backward-compatible in Parquet. Breaking changes need versioned paths.
Always: explicit beats implicit. Config-driven beats hardcoded. Idempotent beats append-only.

viz.note: Senior scoring: 1pt clear problem statement, 1pt named trade-offs (not just options), 1pt concrete example from your work. Generic answers score 1/3.

qa.q: How would you version a dataset schema without breaking existing consumers?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Additive (new nullable columns): Parquet handles automatically -- existing readers see null. Breaking changes: new versioned path (v2/) that new consumers opt into while old consumers stay on v1, or a transition period where both field names coexist before deprecating the old one on a communicated timeline. Never break consumers without a migration path.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Requires understanding the underlying execution engine mechanics, memory layout, and runtime optimization pathways for Cross-stack technical deep dives.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Under high concurrency or large data volume, misconfiguring or misusing How can trigger CPU spikes, memory leaks, or execution bottlenecks.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Balancing execution performance, maintainability, and operational complexity requires explicit architectural evaluation before adoption.

qa.q: How do you test transformation logic without running the full dataset?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Create a representative test dataset: 10-20 rows covering edge cases (nulls, duplicates, boundary values). Write unit tests: given this input, assert this output. pytest + assert_frame_equal for pandas; local SparkSession for PySpark. Test the function in isolation -- integration tests on full pipelines live separately as slower tests.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Spark Driver compiles DataFrame operations into a Catalyst logical plan, optimizes it into a Physical plan, and distributes tasks across Executor JVMs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Data skew on join/group keys forces single executors to spill to disk or fail with OutOfMemory (OOM) errors.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Broadcasting small tables eliminates expensive network shuffles, but broadcasting large tables exhausts Driver memory.
